requirements.quote:
If the
   client opts to do so, it MUST supply both the "pre_shared_key" and
   "early_data" extensions.
requirements.condition: when a client sends Application Data in its first flight using an early-data-capable PSK
requirements.required_behavior: supply the pre_shared_key extension
requirements.why_checkable: The first-flight ClientHello can be inspected for pre_shared_key when early data is sent.

requirements.quote:
If the
   client opts to do so, it MUST supply both the "pre_shared_key" and
   "early_data" extensions.
requirements.condition: when a client sends Application Data in its first flight using an early-data-capable PSK
requirements.required_behavior: supply the early_data extension
requirements.why_checkable: The first-flight ClientHello can be inspected for early_data when early data is sent.

requirements.quote:
The "extension_data" field of this extension contains an
   "EarlyDataIndication" value.
requirements.condition: when encoding an early_data extension
requirements.required_behavior: encode an EarlyDataIndication value in extension_data
requirements.why_checkable: The extension_data payload type is determined by the containing extension.

requirements.condition: when EarlyDataIndication occurs in NewSessionTicket
requirements.required_behavior: encode extension_data as a uint32 max_early_data_size
requirements.why_checkable: The message-type variant and four-octet field can be parsed directly.

requirements.condition: when EarlyDataIndication occurs in ClientHello
requirements.required_behavior: encode extension_data as Empty
requirements.forbidden_behavior: include payload bytes in the EarlyDataIndication
requirements.why_checkable: The ClientHello variant is required to have a zero-length payload.

requirements.condition: when EarlyDataIndication occurs in EncryptedExtensions
requirements.required_behavior: encode extension_data as Empty
requirements.forbidden_behavior: include payload bytes in the EarlyDataIndication
requirements.why_checkable: The EncryptedExtensions variant is required to have a zero-length payload.

requirements.quote:
The parameters for the 0-RTT data (version, symmetric cipher suite,
   Application-Layer Protocol Negotiation (ALPN) [RFC7301] protocol,
   etc.) are those associated with the PSK in use.
requirements.condition: when sending or accepting 0-RTT data
requirements.required_behavior: use the TLS version associated with the PSK in use
requirements.forbidden_behavior: use 0-RTT under a different TLS version
requirements.why_checkable: The 0-RTT version can be compared with PSK metadata.

requirements.quote:
The parameters for the 0-RTT data (version, symmetric cipher suite,
   Application-Layer Protocol Negotiation (ALPN) [RFC7301] protocol,
   etc.) are those associated with the PSK in use.
requirements.condition: when sending or accepting 0-RTT data
requirements.required_behavior: use the symmetric cipher suite associated with the PSK in use
requirements.forbidden_behavior: use 0-RTT under a different symmetric cipher suite
requirements.why_checkable: The 0-RTT cipher suite can be compared with PSK metadata.

requirements.quote:
The parameters for the 0-RTT data (version, symmetric cipher suite,
   Application-Layer Protocol Negotiation (ALPN) [RFC7301] protocol,
   etc.) are those associated with the PSK in use.
requirements.condition: when sending or accepting 0-RTT data with an ALPN protocol
requirements.required_behavior: use the ALPN protocol associated with the PSK in use
requirements.forbidden_behavior: use 0-RTT under a different ALPN protocol
requirements.why_checkable: The 0-RTT ALPN selection can be compared with PSK metadata.

requirements.quote:
For externally
   provisioned PSKs, the associated values are those provisioned along
   with the key.
requirements.condition: when 0-RTT uses an externally provisioned PSK
requirements.required_behavior: obtain the associated 0-RTT parameter values from those provisioned with the key
requirements.why_checkable: The implementation's external-PSK metadata source is concrete and inspectable.

requirements.quote:
For PSKs established via a NewSessionTicket message,
   the associated values are those which were negotiated in the
   connection which established the PSK.
requirements.condition: when 0-RTT uses a PSK established by NewSessionTicket
requirements.required_behavior: obtain the associated 0-RTT parameter values from the connection that established the PSK
requirements.why_checkable: Stored ticket metadata can be compared with the originating connection's negotiation.

requirements.quote:
The PSK used to encrypt the
   early data MUST be the first PSK listed in the client's
   "pre_shared_key" extension.
requirements.condition: when a client encrypts early data
requirements.required_behavior: use the first PSK listed in the client's pre_shared_key extension
requirements.forbidden_behavior: encrypt early data with any later offered PSK
requirements.why_checkable: The early traffic key's source identity can be compared with offer index zero.

requirements.quote:
For PSKs provisioned via NewSessionTicket, a server MUST validate
   that the ticket age for the selected PSK identity (computed by
   subtracting ticket_age_add from PskIdentity.obfuscated_ticket_age
   modulo 2^32) is within a small tolerance of the time since the ticket
   was issued (see Section 8).
requirements.condition: when a server selects a PSK identity provisioned by NewSessionTicket
requirements.required_behavior: compute the ticket age by subtracting ticket_age_add from obfuscated_ticket_age modulo 2^32
requirements.why_checkable: The age formula has fixed uint32 modular arithmetic and concrete input fields.

requirements.quote:
For PSKs provisioned via NewSessionTicket, a server MUST validate
   that the ticket age for the selected PSK identity (computed by
   subtracting ticket_age_add from PskIdentity.obfuscated_ticket_age
   modulo 2^32) is within a small tolerance of the time since the ticket
   was issued (see Section 8).
requirements.condition: when a server selects a PSK identity provisioned by NewSessionTicket
requirements.required_behavior: validate that the computed ticket age is within the server's small tolerance of the time since ticket issuance
requirements.why_checkable: The computed age, issuance time, and configured tolerance provide concrete comparison inputs.

requirements.quote:
If it is not, the server SHOULD proceed
   with the handshake but reject 0-RTT, and SHOULD NOT take any other
   action that assumes that this ClientHello is fresh.
requirements.condition: when the selected ticket's computed age is outside the allowed tolerance
requirements.required_behavior: proceed with the handshake
requirements.why_checkable: The out-of-tolerance branch can be checked for continued non-0-RTT handshake processing.

requirements.quote:
If it is not, the server SHOULD proceed
   with the handshake but reject 0-RTT, and SHOULD NOT take any other
   action that assumes that this ClientHello is fresh.
requirements.condition: when the selected ticket's computed age is outside the allowed tolerance
requirements.required_behavior: reject 0-RTT
requirements.forbidden_behavior: accept the offered early data
requirements.why_checkable: The server's early-data acceptance state is directly observable after age validation.

requirements.quote:
If it is not, the server SHOULD proceed
   with the handshake but reject 0-RTT, and SHOULD NOT take any other
   action that assumes that this ClientHello is fresh.
requirements.condition: when the selected ticket's computed age is outside the allowed tolerance
requirements.forbidden_behavior: take any other action that assumes the ClientHello is fresh
requirements.why_checkable: Freshness-dependent state transitions can be gated on the failed age check.

requirements.quote:
0-RTT messages sent in the first flight have the same (encrypted)
   content types as messages of the same type sent in other flights
   (handshake and application_data) but are protected under different
   keys.
requirements.condition: when encoding a 0-RTT handshake or application-data message in the first flight
requirements.required_behavior: use the same encrypted content type as the corresponding message type in other flights
requirements.why_checkable: The outer and inner record content types are directly parseable.

requirements.quote:
0-RTT messages sent in the first flight have the same (encrypted)
   content types as messages of the same type sent in other flights
   (handshake and application_data) but are protected under different
   keys.
requirements.condition: when protecting a 0-RTT message in the first flight
requirements.required_behavior: protect it under the 0-RTT keys rather than the keys used for corresponding later-flight messages
requirements.forbidden_behavior: protect it under the corresponding later-flight traffic keys
requirements.why_checkable: Record-key selection is tied to the flight and can be traced in the record protection path.

requirements.quote:
After receiving the server's Finished message, if the server
   has accepted early data, an EndOfEarlyData message will be sent to
   indicate the key change.
requirements.condition: after the client receives the server Finished and the server has accepted early data
requirements.required_behavior: send an EndOfEarlyData message to indicate the key change
requirements.why_checkable: Handshake message order can be checked after early-data acceptance.

requirements.quote:
This message will be encrypted with the
   0-RTT traffic keys.
requirements.condition: when sending EndOfEarlyData after accepted early data
requirements.required_behavior: encrypt EndOfEarlyData with the 0-RTT traffic keys
requirements.why_checkable: The record protection epoch used for EndOfEarlyData can be inspected.

requirements.quote:
A server which receives an "early_data" extension MUST behave in one
   of three ways:
requirements.condition: when a server receives an early_data extension
requirements.required_behavior: choose one of the three defined behaviors: ignore early data and continue with 1-RTT, send HelloRetryRequest and ignore early data, or accept early data by returning early_data in EncryptedExtensions
requirements.forbidden_behavior: use a response behavior outside the three defined alternatives
requirements.why_checkable: The server response and subsequent record-processing branch identify one of the enumerated alternatives.

requirements.quote: Ignore the extension and return a regular 1-RTT response.
requirements.condition: when the server chooses the first defined response to an early_data extension
requirements.required_behavior: ignore the extension and return a regular 1-RTT response
requirements.why_checkable: The response omits early-data acceptance and follows the regular 1-RTT path.

requirements.quote:
The
      server then skips past early data by attempting to deprotect
      received records using the handshake traffic key, discarding
      records which fail deprotection (up to the configured
      max_early_data_size).
requirements.condition: when the server ignores early_data and returns a regular 1-RTT response
requirements.required_behavior: attempt to deprotect received records with the handshake traffic key
requirements.why_checkable: The trial-deprotection loop's selected traffic key is concrete implementation state.

requirements.quote:
The
      server then skips past early data by attempting to deprotect
      received records using the handshake traffic key, discarding
      records which fail deprotection (up to the configured
      max_early_data_size).
requirements.condition: when a received record fails handshake-key deprotection while the server skips rejected early data
requirements.required_behavior: discard the failed record
requirements.forbidden_behavior: treat the failed record as the start of the client's second flight
requirements.why_checkable: Failed trial deprotection has a concrete discard branch.

requirements.quote:
The
      server then skips past early data by attempting to deprotect
      received records using the handshake traffic key, discarding
      records which fail deprotection (up to the configured
      max_early_data_size).
requirements.condition: when the server discards records that fail handshake-key deprotection while skipping rejected early data
requirements.required_behavior: enforce configured max_early_data_size as the discard limit
requirements.forbidden_behavior: continue discarding failed records beyond configured max_early_data_size
requirements.why_checkable: The trial-deprotection loop has a concrete configured byte limit.

requirements.quote:
Once a record is deprotected successfully,
      it is treated as the start of the client's second flight and the
      server proceeds as with an ordinary 1-RTT handshake.
requirements.condition: when a record first deprotects successfully while the server skips rejected early data using the handshake traffic key
requirements.required_behavior: treat that record as the start of the client's second flight
requirements.why_checkable: The first successful deprotection identifies a concrete flight-boundary transition.

requirements.quote:
Once a record is deprotected successfully,
      it is treated as the start of the client's second flight and the
      server proceeds as with an ordinary 1-RTT handshake.
requirements.condition: after the server successfully deprotects the first non-0-RTT record with the handshake traffic key
requirements.required_behavior: proceed as an ordinary 1-RTT handshake
requirements.why_checkable: The successful deprotection branch has a prescribed handshake processing path.

requirements.quote:
Request that the client send another ClientHello by responding
      with a HelloRetryRequest.
requirements.condition: when the server chooses the second defined response to an early_data extension
requirements.required_behavior: respond with HelloRetryRequest to request another ClientHello
requirements.why_checkable: The server's response message type and expected client transition are directly observable.

requirements.quote:
A client MUST NOT include the
      "early_data" extension in its followup ClientHello.
requirements.condition: when a client sends a followup ClientHello after HelloRetryRequest
requirements.forbidden_behavior: include the early_data extension
requirements.why_checkable: The second ClientHello extension list can be inspected.

requirements.quote:
The server
      then ignores early data by skipping all records with an external
      content type of "application_data" (indicating that they are
      encrypted), up to the configured max_early_data_size.
requirements.condition: when the server sends HelloRetryRequest in response to an early_data extension
requirements.required_behavior: skip all records with external content type application_data
requirements.forbidden_behavior: process the skipped records as accepted early data
requirements.why_checkable: The record content-type loop has a concrete skip predicate.

requirements.quote:
The server
      then ignores early data by skipping all records with an external
      content type of "application_data" (indicating that they are
      encrypted), up to the configured max_early_data_size.
requirements.condition: when the server skips external application_data records after sending HelloRetryRequest
requirements.required_behavior: enforce configured max_early_data_size as the skip limit
requirements.forbidden_behavior: continue skipping application_data records beyond configured max_early_data_size
requirements.why_checkable: The record-skip loop has a concrete configured byte limit.

requirements.quote:
Return its own "early_data" extension in EncryptedExtensions,
      indicating that it intends to process the early data.
requirements.condition: when the server chooses to accept and process early data
requirements.required_behavior: return an early_data extension in EncryptedExtensions
requirements.why_checkable: Server early-data acceptance is signaled by a specific extension in a specific message.

requirements.quote:
It is not
      possible for the server to accept only a subset of the early data
      messages.
requirements.condition: when the server accepts early data
requirements.required_behavior: accept the early-data messages as a whole
requirements.forbidden_behavior: accept only a subset of the early-data messages
requirements.why_checkable: The server's early-data processing path can be checked for partial-acceptance behavior.

requirements.quote:
In order to accept early data, the server MUST have accepted a PSK
   cipher suite and selected the first key offered in the client's
   "pre_shared_key" extension.
requirements.condition: when a server accepts early data
requirements.required_behavior: have accepted a PSK cipher suite
requirements.forbidden_behavior: accept early data without a PSK cipher suite
requirements.why_checkable: The negotiated cipher-suite path can be checked before setting early-data acceptance.

requirements.quote:
In order to accept early data, the server MUST have accepted a PSK
   cipher suite and selected the first key offered in the client's
   "pre_shared_key" extension.
requirements.condition: when a server accepts early data
requirements.required_behavior: select the first key offered in the client's pre_shared_key extension
requirements.forbidden_behavior: accept early data using any later offered key
requirements.why_checkable: The selected_identity can be checked for index zero.

requirements.quote:
In addition, it MUST verify that the
   following values are the same as those associated with the
   selected PSK:

   -  The TLS version number
requirements.condition: when a server considers accepting early data
requirements.required_behavior: verify that the TLS version number is the same as the version associated with the selected PSK
requirements.forbidden_behavior: accept early data with a mismatched TLS version
requirements.why_checkable: The negotiated version and stored PSK version are concrete comparison operands.

requirements.quote:
In addition, it MUST verify that the
   following values are the same as those associated with the
   selected PSK:

   -  The TLS version number

   -  The selected cipher suite
requirements.condition: when a server considers accepting early data
requirements.required_behavior: verify that the selected cipher suite is the same as the cipher suite associated with the selected PSK
requirements.forbidden_behavior: accept early data with a mismatched cipher suite
requirements.why_checkable: The selected cipher suite and stored PSK cipher suite are concrete comparison operands.

requirements.quote:
In addition, it MUST verify that the
   following values are the same as those associated with the
   selected PSK:

   -  The TLS version number

   -  The selected cipher suite

   -  The selected ALPN [RFC7301] protocol, if any
requirements.condition: when a server considers accepting early data and an ALPN protocol is selected
requirements.required_behavior: verify that the selected ALPN protocol is the same as the ALPN protocol associated with the selected PSK
requirements.forbidden_behavior: accept early data with a mismatched ALPN protocol
requirements.why_checkable: The selected ALPN value and stored PSK ALPN value are concrete comparison operands.

requirements.quote:
If any of these checks fail, the server MUST NOT respond with the
   extension
requirements.condition: when any early-data acceptance check fails
requirements.forbidden_behavior: respond with the early_data extension
requirements.why_checkable: Failed acceptance checks directly gate emission of the server extension.

requirements.quote:
If any of these checks fail, the server MUST NOT respond with the
   extension and must discard all the first-flight data using one of the
   first two mechanisms listed above (thus falling back to 1-RTT or
   2-RTT).
requirements.condition: when any early-data acceptance check fails
requirements.required_behavior: discard all first-flight data using the regular 1-RTT trial-deprotection mechanism or the HelloRetryRequest skip mechanism
requirements.forbidden_behavior: process any first-flight data as accepted early data
requirements.why_checkable: The rejection branch has two enumerated discard procedures and a prescribed fallback.

requirements.quote:
If the client attempts a 0-RTT handshake but the server
   rejects it, the server will generally not have the 0-RTT record
   protection keys and must instead use trial decryption (either with
   the 1-RTT handshake keys or by looking for a cleartext ClientHello in
   the case of a HelloRetryRequest) to find the first non-0-RTT message.
requirements.condition: when the client attempts 0-RTT, the server rejects it, and the server lacks the 0-RTT record protection keys
requirements.required_behavior: use trial decryption with the 1-RTT handshake keys or look for a cleartext ClientHello after HelloRetryRequest to find the first non-0-RTT message
requirements.why_checkable: The rejected-0-RTT record scan has explicitly defined key and message alternatives.

requirements.quote:
If the server chooses to accept the "early_data" extension, then it
   MUST comply with the same error-handling requirements specified for
   all records when processing early data records.
requirements.condition: when a server accepts early_data and processes early-data records
requirements.required_behavior: apply the error-handling requirements specified for all records
requirements.forbidden_behavior: apply weaker record error handling because a record is early data
requirements.error_behavior: use the standard record error-handling paths
requirements.why_checkable: The early-record path can be compared with the ordinary record failure paths.

requirements.quote:
Specifically, if the
   server fails to decrypt a 0-RTT record following an accepted
   "early_data" extension, it MUST terminate the connection with a
   "bad_record_mac" alert as per Section 5.2.
requirements.condition: when a server fails to decrypt a 0-RTT record after accepting early_data
requirements.required_behavior: terminate the connection
requirements.forbidden_behavior: discard the undecryptable record and continue the connection
requirements.error_behavior: terminate the connection with a bad_record_mac alert
requirements.why_checkable: A decryption failure after acceptance has a specific alert and terminal outcome.
